land.text: the right bank of the Danube in Pannonia, the lands Constantine granted to the Vandals after Geberic's Goths attacked them

predecessors.note: The page dates the grant to Constantine's reign (he died in 337); Cliopatria's first Vandal shape begins in 337.

land.text: the Mauretanian and Numidian lands Gaiseric conquered from 429 and kept under the 435 treaty ('Mauretania and part of Numidia as foederati')

successors.note: The vandal-kingdom dossier starts in 435 (treaty with Valentinian III) with its capital at Hippo Regius; this dossier ends the year before so the two never overlap. Cliopatria's Vandals row runs to 438 but is drawn in Baetica, which the Vandals left in 429.

capitals.name: Hippo Regius (Annaba)
capitals.note: The page says Gaiseric seized Hippo Regius unopposed in 432 and 'made it the first capital of the Vandal kingdom'. Before 429 the Vandals had no seat: a people on the move (Pannonia, Gaul, Hispania). Carthage follows after 439 in vandal-kingdom.

rulers.name: Godigisel
rulers.title: king of the Hasdingi
rulers.note: Killed in the war with the Franks before or at the Rhine crossing (Crossing of the Rhine page: the Vandals lost 'about 20,000 warriors, including King Godigisel').

rulers.name: Gunderic
rulers.title: king of the Hasdingi, from 419 also of the Silingi and Alans
rulers.note: The Vandals page names him leading the Vandals through Gaul and Spain and dying at Seville in 428; the 407 accession and the 428 end are from the Gunderic page (a sixth page, see sources).

rulers.name: Gaiseric (Genseric)
rulers.title: king of the Vandals and Alans
rulers.note: Reign continues to 477 in vandal-kingdom; cut here at 434.

keyframe_review.note: 31,881 km2 on the Danube in Pannonia (Austria, Hungary, Slovakia). The page: after Geberic's Goths attacked, Constantine 'granted them lands on the right bank of the Danube'. The shape also reaches the left bank (Slovakia); the page names only the right bank. No infobox area to compare.

Same Pannonian shape; the page dates no change of land between the Constantinian grant and 405/406, and Aurelian's c. 271 peace and Probus's 278 defeat lie before the shape begins. Unverified: page budget.
Same Pannonian shape; no dated change on the page (Stilicho's time: a raid on Raetia in the winter of 401/402, not a change of land). Unverified: page budget.

Same Pannonian shape until the move west. The page has the Vandals 'advance from Pannonia' in 405 (it gives 31 December 405 for the Rhine crossing; the Crossing of the Rhine page says 'traditionally 31 December 406' and notes Kulikowski's 405); the ledger leaves Pannonia in 406.

correction.text: Gaul as the Vandals ravaged it from the Rhine crossing (31 December 406) to the Pyrenees crossing (October 409); the Cliopatria shape without its German and Bohemian part east of the Rhine

keyframe_review.note: 91,608 km2, a band from Belgium and northern France across Germany to 18.8 E. The crossing of the Rhine (31 December 406) put the Vandals in Gaul; the part east of the Rhine (Germany, Czechia, Poland: 6.6-18.8 E) is the road they had already left. The page: they ravaged Gaul, 'Aquitaine, Novempopulania, Lugdunensis, and Narbonensis' by c. 409 (Jerome), though Kulikowski has them mostly in northern Gaul until spring 409. Keep the France and Belgium part; the path of devastation is not a border, so the shape stays a presence zone.

correction.text: the Hasdingi's north-west (Gallaecia) and the Silingi's south (Baetica), 410 only: not the whole peninsula, whose Tarraco court was Maximus's

keyframe_review.note: 420,482 km2: the whole Iberian peninsula (-9.4 to 0.1 E). The page has the Vandals crossing the Pyrenees on 13 October 409 and, around the same time, the Hasdingi taking the north-west and the Silingi the south. As a plunder zone for 410 the peninsula stands; from 411 the Hasdingi page (Gerontius's allotment of 411) confines them to the lands of the new keyframe vandals_411. The other barbarian peoples share the peninsula (Alans, Suebi: Cliopatria draws them separately from 414). Repair fx-28: the whole-peninsula 'plunder zone' overlapped Maximus's Hispania (670 cells in 410, 839 in 411). The Vandals page (opened again) has the crossing 'On October 13, 409' and names only two Vandal lands, 'the Hasdingi received land from the Romans, as foederati, in Asturia (Northwest)' and 'the Silingi in Hispania Baetica (South)'; it does not date them to 410 and has the Alans in Lusitania and around Carthago Nova, so the 410 shape is cut to the two lands the page names.

correction.text: eastern Gallaecia (the Hasdingi) and Baetica (the Silingi)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 95,849 km2 of Cliopatria's own 414-416 shape, brought forward to 411. The Hasdingi page: Gerontius 'in 411 agreed to allocate large parts of Hispania to several barbarian peoples'; 'The Hasdingi settled in eastern Gallaecia', the Suebi to their west; the Silingi page: 'the Silingi settled in Baetica'. The rest of the peninsula goes to the Alans (see alans) and the Suebi.

Cliopatria's 414-416 shape (Baetica 63,700 km2 plus Galicia 21,500 km2, 102,797 km2 in all) is the 411 allotment: eastern Gallaecia to the Hasdingi, Baetica to the Silingi. Both halves are separate Vandal groups until 419 (Silingi page: they joined Gunderic after the Gothic attacks of 417-18).

correction.text: unchanged shape (Baetica), valid for 419-425 only: Gunderic's Hasdingi and the Silingi and Alan remnants who submitted to him

keyframe_review.note: 68,460 km2 around Baetica, drawn 417-425 as if the Silingi still held it. The page: the Visigoths 'crushed the Silingi Vandals in 417'; the Hasdingi stay in Gallaecia until 'In 419 ... Gunderic fled to Baetica' after a Roman-Suebi defeat (the Hasdingi page puts the defeat in 419-420, the Gunderic page the move in 420-1). So the shape holds from 419 only; for 417-418 the Vandals hold eastern Gallaecia alone (vandals_417b). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 419..425 from this entry's own 'valid for 419-425 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: eastern Gallaecia, the Hasdingi's allotment, while the Visigoths destroy the Silingi in Baetica

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: with the Silingi crushed in 417 and the Alans in 418, the Vandals' only land is the Hasdingi's eastern Gallaecia until Gunderic's flight to Baetica in 419.

correction.text: unchanged shape (Baetica), valid for 426-428 only: the last years in Spain under Gunderic and then Gaiseric

keyframe_review.note: 68,460 km2 in Baetica for 426-438, but the page has the Vandals leave Spain in 429 ('Gaiseric decided to leave Hispania to his rivals'; 'the Vandals departed Spain' in 429 on the Vandals page). The shape is right for 426-428 only (Gunderic took Seville again in 428 and died there; Gaiseric succeeded). From 429 the land is Mauretania and Numidia (vandals_429); from 435 it is the vandal-kingdom dossier's. Review fx-28: to set to 428, as the correction text says (data/shapes.csv runs the shape to 438, so in 429 it was still alive beside vandals_429 and the union drew Baetica back after ledger 12). Vandals page: 'In 429 ... the Vandals entered North Africa'.

correction.text: Mauretania and Numidia, overrun after the crossing of 429 and held under the 435 treaty; without Hippo Regius until its fall in 432

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Gaiseric's forces quickly overran the territory now comprising modern Morocco and northern Algeria' after the 429 crossing; the 435 treaty then recognised him in 'Mauretania and part of Numidia'. The page dates neither province's fall, so the whole of both is drawn from 429 as a presence zone (soft). Hippo Regius falls in 432 on the Vandals page (the Gaiseric page says 'after 14 months', 430-31). Review fx-28: Hippo Regius (Annaba, 60 km) taken out of the 429 shape: the Vandals page has Genseric 'seize Hippo Regius unopposed' 'During the summer of 432' (ledger 14 gains it then); the whole-Numidia region handed it over in 429 and made ledger 14 and western-roman-empire ledger 22 empty.

region.text: the right bank of the Danube in Pannonia

ledger.note: 337: the Vandals hold the Pannonian lands Constantine granted them. 'Constantine granted them lands on the right bank of the Danube' after Geberic's Goths attacked and Visimar was killed; the page puts the grant in Constantine's reign (he died in 337), no year.

region.text: the Danube lands in Pannonia the Vandals held since Constantine

ledger.note: 406: the Vandals leave Pannonia for the Rhine. The page has them 'advance from Pannonia' in 405 (it gives 31 December 405 for the crossing; the Crossing page prefers 406).

region.text: Gaul as the Vandals ravaged it: France and Belgium

ledger.note: 406: the Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the frozen Rhine. 'Vandals and Alans came into the Gauls, having crossed the Rhine, on the day before the kalends of January' (Prosper): the crossing 'is traditionally considered to have occurred on 31 December 406', near Mainz; Kulikowski argues for 31 December 405.

region.text: Gaul as the Vandals ravaged it: France and Belgium

ledger.note: 409: the Vandals leave Gaul for Spain. Jerome's letter of c. 409 lists the ravaged provinces of Aquitaine, Novempopulania, Lugdunensis and Narbonensis; 'Hydatius dated the barbarian entry into Spain to September or October 409'.

region.text: the Hasdingi's north-west (Gallaecia) and the Silingi's south (Baetica), the lands the Vandals held in Hispania (not the whole peninsula)

ledger.note: 409: the Vandals cross the Pyrenees into Hispania. They 'crossed the Pyrenees into the Iberian peninsula' on 13 October 409 (Vandals page; the Gunderic page and Hydatius say October or September-October 409). Repair fx-28: region cut from the whole peninsula to the Hasdingi's north-west and the Silingi's south, the only Vandal lands the Vandals page names ('Asturia (Northwest)'; 'Hispania Baetica (South)'); the rest of Hispania was Maximus's Tarraco court (Maximus page) and the Alans' Lusitania.

411: Gerontius allots Hispania to the barbarians. He 'agreed to allocate large parts of Hispania to several barbarian peoples' (Hasdingi page): 'The Hasdingi settled in eastern Gallaecia', the Suebi to their west; 'the Silingi settled in Baetica' (Silingi page, no year). The Alans take Lusitania and Carthaginensis (alans).

417: the Silingi lose Baetica. 'Following Roman-sponsored attacks by the Visigoths against the Silingi in 417-18' the survivors changed allegiance; the Vandals page has the Visigoths 'crush the Silingi Vandals in 417'. The land stays a Roman province (the pages do not say who held it until Gunderic arrived).

417: the Visigoths fall on the Silingi in Baetica. 'Roman-sponsored attacks by the Visigoths against the Silingi in 417-18' (Silingi page); the Visigoths 'crushed the Silingi Vandals in 417 and the Alans in 418' (Vandals page).

418: the Gothic campaign ends; the Silingi are destroyed. The survivors 'changed allegiance' after the attacks (Silingi page); the Vandals page has the Visigoths crush the Silingi in 417 and the Alans in 418. Who holds Baetica afterwards the pages do not say (Roman province).

region.text: Gunderic's Hasdingi in Gallaecia, whom the Alan survivors joined

ledger.note: 418: the Alan survivors accept Gunderic. 'The Alans joined in 418. After their king Attaces fell in battle against the Visigoths in Hispania, most surviving Alans appealed to Gunderic, who accepted them'; he is then 'King of Vandals and Alans (418-428)'. The Silingi page has 'the remnants of the Silingi and the Alans voluntarily submitted to the Hasdingian leader Gunderic' in 419.
419: the Hasdingi are driven from Gallaecia. 'The Hasdingi were defeated by a Roman-Suebi coalition. Gunderic fled to Baetica'; the Hasdingi page puts the Roman relief of the Suebi in 419-420.
419: Gunderic takes Baetica. He 'fled to Baetica, where he was also proclaimed king of the Silingi Vandals'; the land is the Silingi's emptied allotment (the page does not say who held it after 418).

429: the Vandals leave Spain. 'not long after taking power, Gaiseric decided to leave Hispania to his rivals'; 'the Vandals departed Spain' in 429 (Vandals page). The page does not say who took Baetica; a Suebi force took Lusitania and was beaten at Mérida (428).

region.text: Mauretania and Numidia without Hippo Regius

ledger.note: 429: the Vandals land in Africa. Gaiseric led 'most of his people' (80,000 in the tradition, 50,000 on Heather's reckoning) and his forces 'quickly overran the territory now comprising modern Morocco and northern Algeria'; no dates for the provinces. Review fx-28: Hippo Regius left out: it falls 'During the summer of 432' (Vandals page), ledger 14.

region.text: Hippo Regius, besieged from 430 (Augustine died on 28 August 430, three months into the siege)

ledger.note: 432: the Vandals take Hippo Regius. After defeating Bonifacius and Aspar, Genseric 'seize[d] Hippo Regius unopposed' and 'made it the first capital of the Vandal kingdom' (Vandals page; the Gaiseric page has the siege last 14 months, so 430-31).
432: Hippo Regius becomes the Vandal seat (Carthage follows after 19 October 439, in vandal-kingdom).

region.text: Mauretania and the Numidian lands held in 434

ledger.note: 434: the wandering Vandals become the Vandal Kingdom the next year. The 435 treaty with Valentinian III recognised Gaiseric 'as king of the lands he had conquered'; 'the Vandals also kept Mauretania and part of Numidia as foederati'. The year 434 is the researcher's cut so that this dossier and vandal-kingdom (from 435) do not overlap.

wars.name: Vandal raid on Raetia
wars.outcome: A raid with no lasting land: 'Vandals raided the Roman province of Raetia in the winter of 401/402'.
wars.note: Stilicho, described as of Vandal descent, commanded Rome's armies.

wars.name: Frankish war and crossing of the Rhine

zones.text: the Rhine at Mogontiacum (Mainz) and the Gaul beyond

wars.outcome: The Franks fought the Vandals and were winning (the Vandals lost 'about 20,000 warriors, including King Godigisel') until the Alans came to the Vandals' aid and defeated the Franks 'in a decisive battle'; the Vandals, Alans and Suebi then crossed the Rhine on 31 December 406.
wars.note: Frigeridus's fragment gives no date or place for the battle; Kulikowski dates the crossing to 31 December 405.

wars.name: Vandal ravaging of Gaul and the move to Hispania

zones.text: Gaul as the Vandals ravaged it: France and Belgium

wars.outcome: No land is held: the Vandals 'plundered their way westward and southward through Aquitaine' and crossed the Pyrenees on 13 October 409.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign against the Silingi and Alans
wars.outcome: The Visigoths, as Roman federates, 'crushed the Silingi Vandals in 417 and the Alans in 418', then were recalled to Aquitaine; the Hasdingi in Gallaecia were untouched.

wars.name: Vandal-Suebi war in Gallaecia
wars.outcome: The Hasdingi attacked the Suebi, Roman forces under Asterius relieved the Suebi and 'defeated the Vandals in battle' in 419-420; Gunderic fled to Baetica.
wars.note: The Vandals page dates the defeat to 419; the Gunderic page puts the move into Baetica in 420-1.

wars.name: Battle against Castinus
wars.outcome: Gunderic 'decisively defeated' a Roman-Suebi-Gothic coalition led by Castinus; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Vandal raids on the Balearics, Hispania and Mauretania
wars.outcome: The Vandals sacked Cartagena and Seville and left; Gunderic retook Seville in 428 and died besieging its church.
wars.note: Neither city was held (Gunderic page: 'did not remain in these cities').

wars.name: Vandal conquest of Mauretania and Numidia
wars.outcome: Gaiseric overran Mauretania and Numidia, beat Bonifacius at Calama, took Hippo Regius after the siege of 430-32, and was recognised in 435 as king of the lands he held ('Mauretania and part of Numidia as foederati').
wars.note: Carthage falls on 19 October 439, outside this dossier.

certainty.note: A people on the move: Danube settlement, a devastation zone in Gaul, the 411 allotment lines in Hispania and the African conquest are all approximate; the first treaty line (435) belongs to vandal-kingdom.

notes:
Cliopatria's Vandals row (337-438, nine shapes) is read as: Pannonia 337-405, Gaul 407-409, the whole peninsula 410-413, the 411 allotment (Galicia plus Baetica) 414-416, then Baetica to 438. Corrections: the 407 shape loses its German half; 410 is a one-year plunder zone; 411-413 is the allotment; 417-418 only Gallaecia (the Silingi are destroyed); 426-428 Baetica; 429-434 Mauretania and Numidia; 435-438 belong to vandal-kingdom (start 435), which this dossier hands over to by ending in 434. The Vandals have no capital until Hippo Regius (432), so identity.capitals starts then. Family 'africa' follows vandal-kingdom for colour continuity.
Page disagreements: Rhine crossing 31 Dec 405 (Vandals page, Kulikowski) or 406 (Crossing page, tradition; used); Gunderic's move to Baetica 419 (Vandals page; used), 419-420 (Hasdingi page), 420-1 (Gunderic page); Hippo Regius taken in 431 (14-month siege, Gaiseric page) or 432 (Vandals page; used); 80,000 people (tradition) or 50,000 (Heather).
Budget: five pages (Vandals, Crossing of the Rhine, Silingi, Hasdingi, Gaiseric). The Gunderic page was read for the Alans dossier and is a sixth source here, one over the budget, used only for Gunderic's reign (407-428), the 418 and 420-1 dates and Seville in 425 and 428. Unverified: 358-394 shapes (unchanged Pannonia). The Hasdingi page does not mention Nervasian hills or Seville; the Vandals page does not mention 411. The Suebi (kingdom-of-the-suebi) are the counterpart of the 419 Gallaecia loss; the Alans (alans) of the 419 merger. The Silingi and Hasdingi have no dossier of their own; a gap-filler could split them (Silingi 409-419) but Cliopatria draws one row.
